settings.heading: Reviving abandoned pockets of Tuscan land, one harvest at a time.

settings.long_text: The 2026 harvest is here, in a 250ml can. Fresh Tuscan extra virgin olive oil, cold pressed and made in small batches. It travels well and makes a good gift for anyone who cooks. Order by 16 December for UK Christmas delivery.
settings.asset_alt: The UNTO 250ml olive oil tin with olives, a clementine and rosemary on a lime background

settings.section_text: Unto was started as a rural recovery project with the goal to bring life back to neglected pockets of Tuscan land. These fertile grounds sustained rich agriculture for centuries but fell into abandonment following rural depopulation since the ’50s. It is in this setting that our independent farming community was born. Producing a range of superior quality olive oils is the first step on our journey to restore and revive the land and our heritage. Join us.

settings.text: A tin weighs far less than a glass bottle, so it costs less to post and won't break on the way.
Light is what spoils olive oil. Inside a tin it's always dark, so the oil stays fresh for longer.
Steel recycles again and again. Rinse the tin and put it in your household recycling.

settings.heading: Our goal: bring life back to neglected pockets of Tuscan land.
settings.text: UNTO started as a rural recovery project in the hills of Florence. The land fed people for centuries, then emptied out from the 1950s. We work with small farms to keep it producing, starting with olive oil.

settings.q: Can I send it as a gift?
settings.a:
Yes. Add a gift message in your cart and enter their address at checkout.

Sending to several people? Place one order per address.

settings.q: What do I do with it?
settings.a: Pour it on things. Warm bread, beans, soup, roast potatoes, a fried egg. Add it at the end, off the heat.
New-season Tuscan oil is green and grassy, with a peppery kick at the back of the throat. The pepper is a sign of fresh oil, and it softens over the months.
The best-before date is printed on the tin. Keep it somewhere cool and dark. It's at its best young, so don't save it for a special occasion.

settings.q: Where does the oil come from?
settings.a: From a small farm in the hills around Florence. UNTO started as a project to bring neglected Tuscan land back into use. Read the story.
Italian for new oil: the first oil of the season, pressed in autumn, at its greenest and most peppery. In Tuscany people wait all year for it.
